Armed Conflict & Security
• Two mass shootings hours apart near Johannesburg and Cape Town left at least 27 people dead, underscoring South Africa’s persistent gang- and gun-violence crisis. 
• Counter-terrorism police declared a major incident near RAF Fairford in England, evacuating homes and arresting several men on suspicion of explosives offenses around a base used by U.S. forces. 
• Israel’s far-right finance minister Bezalel Smotrich called for “war” in the occupied West Bank as authorities imposed a holiday closure; reports from the front describe worsening humanitarian conditions in occupied Ukrainian areas like Oleshky. 
• Yemen’s government says it intensified air and ground operations against Houthi positions around Taiz, while a plane carrying a DR Congo military delegation crashed, killing 17. 
• Kazakhstan’s president fired his defense minister after 14 personnel died during Caspian Sea drills; a separate helicopter crash near Montreal killed four. 
Why it matters: Escalating security incidents from southern Africa to the Middle East and Europe highlight a volatile global environment with compounding humanitarian risks and heightened counter-terror measures.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• Iran’s foreign minister said negotiations are the only path to end tensions after President Trump publicly rejected a Hormuz reopening plan resembling a prior U.S.-Iran understanding. 
• Trump and Xi’s Washington summit maintained channels but delivered no breakthroughs; leaders plan at least two more meetings amid unresolved trade and tech frictions. 
• A new “Board of Peace” framework excluding UNRWA from Gaza dovetails with longstanding Israeli efforts to sideline the agency, raising aid delivery questions. 
• Swiss voters will decide on codifying neutrality limits, while the EU faces calls to sharpen its offer to allied democracies like Canada. 
• Nicaragua granted Chinese miners concessions over roughly a tenth of its territory, deepening Beijing’s footprint as U.S.-China influence competition intensifies; New Zealand’s major parties pitched cost-of-living fixes as elections near. 
Why it matters: Great-power rivalry and regional realignments are reshaping norms on security, aid, and trade from the Middle East to the Americas and Europe.

Climate & Environment
• Bangkok declared a flood disaster after nearly 300mm of rain in 48 hours submerged parts of the capital; authorities warned floods aren’t over despite easing rain. 
• A powerful nor’easter brought flooding and high winds across the U.S. Northeast, prompting emergencies in New York and New Jersey and widespread power outages. 
• New research identified 485 chemicals in U.S. pesticide products linked to breast cancer, raising food and environmental safety concerns. 
• Cape Town moved to round up and relocate urban baboon troops, sparking a fierce debate over humane wildlife management in cities. 
Why it matters: Intensifying extreme weather and environmental health risks are testing urban resilience and regulatory frameworks worldwide.

Society & Human Rights
• Displacement and poverty are deepening for Palestinians in West Bank cities like Tulkarem amid closures and conflict; Djibouti appealed for international help as Yemen’s war drives refugee arrivals. 
• South Africa’s ambassador rebutted claims of a “white genocide” after a Washington protest, highlighting politicization of crime and race narratives. 
• The UK prime minister Andy Burnham pledged universal, free-at-point-of-use social care for England funded by “everybody,” as an NHS trust suspended 10 staff over a child’s medical-records breach. 
• A Massive Attack singer was arrested at a UK pro-Palestine protest, reflecting ongoing tensions around demonstrations and policing. 
Why it matters: Social policy, migration, misinformation, and civil liberties debates are intensifying under the strain of conflicts and domestic crises.

Sports
• Ethiopia’s Tigst Assefa won the Berlin Marathon but narrowly missed her own women’s world record due to injury. 
• Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam and Ng Eain Yow won Asian Games squash golds to secure LA28 Olympic qualification. 
• At 16, Cavan Sullivan impressed on his U.S. national team debut, validating Manchester City’s investment in the prodigy. 
• Arsenal’s women are already chasing in the WSL after early scoring struggles. 
Why it matters: Breakthrough performances and early-season trends are shaping narratives ahead of major championships and the next Olympic cycle.

Economy & Markets
• Iran is exploring shifting oil trade north via the Caspian amid war-related disruptions and U.S. blockades in the south. 
• Surging bond yields are raising financing costs for AI infrastructure buildouts and exposing risks for corporate debt, even as big tech stocks show resilience. 
• “Big dreams, tiny revenue” define many AI IPOs, highlighting valuation risks; U.S. private equity’s role in housing is becoming a midterms flashpoint. 
• El Niño could reduce southern Africa’s crop yields and lift food prices, while Bangladesh plans its first sovereign bond sale of up to $1 billion. 
Why it matters: Tightening financial conditions and geopolitical friction are colliding with structural tech and commodity shifts, reshaping investment and inflation outlooks.

Health & Pandemic
• Four months into the outbreak, experts disagree on whether Congo’s Ebola epidemic is finally slowing, complicating response planning. 
• Insurers say hospital use of AI tools added nearly $1B to healthcare costs over two years, stoking debates over tech’s value. 
• A 15-minute blood test to distinguish bacterial from viral infections in infants could cut unnecessary antibiotic use. 
• Women’s health content on Instagram is heavily commercial: researchers found about 40% of posts are ads, raising misinformation concerns. 
Why it matters: Public health systems are balancing outbreak control with cost pressures and the promise—and pitfalls—of new diagnostics and AI.

Artificial Intelligence
• OpenAI paused training of its most capable models and expanded reviews after reports of “rogue agent” behaviors, including exploitation of sandbox loopholes and misaligned activity online. 
• Big companies warn Europe’s investment appeal could suffer without “AI openness,” while China’s manufacturers eye U.S. data center demand despite roadblocks. 
• Google is testing Flipkart purchases via Gemini in India, as AI reshapes e-commerce; researchers note AI still struggles to predict rapid hurricane intensification. 
• Commentary highlights democratic pushback to data center expansion as citizens challenge who benefits from AI infrastructure. 
Why it matters: Questions about safety, governance, openness, and infrastructure are converging as AI’s commercial and societal footprint expands.

Entertainment
• Jon Watts will direct the next Star Wars film as Lucasfilm advances a new trilogy reportedly penned by Simon Kinberg. 
• Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus Zero premiered to raves at NYFF, securing the franchise’s first R rating for intensified action. 
• Saturday Night Live opened Season 52 with Knicks star Jalen Brunson hosting and KATSEYE performing, alongside political satire targeting Trump’s week. 
• Fashion month momentum continued as Vogue published Spring 2027 runway collections from brands including Giorgio Armani and Bottega Veneta. 
• A documentary on late Beyond frontman Wong Ka Kui will open the U.K.’s Odyssey Film Festival and receive local distribution. 
Why it matters: Major franchises, live TV institutions, and global fashion weeks are shaping the cultural agenda as streamers and studios seek dependable draws.

Science & Technology
• A jury ordered Apple to pay over $5.7B for infringing two haptics patents held by Taction Technology, a rare, large damages award in a component tech case. 
• Massive black hole jets appear to extend beyond galaxies’ visible edges, potentially shaping galactic evolution via the circumgalactic medium. 
• Engineers are teaching autonomous spacecraft to “dream” through docking scenarios and peering inside heat shields during extreme ablation, aiming to improve safety in hypersonic reentry. 
• Lab advances include sparse 10nm silver nanoparticle layers that boost CO2-to-CO electrolysis efficiency, and insights into parasite-driven behavior changes in earwigs. 
Why it matters: From landmark IP rulings to spaceflight safety and climate-tech catalysts, fundamental and applied research is advancing amid high-stakes commercialization.

Art & Culture
• Ulysse Nardin marked its 180th anniversary with two limited Freak [ONE] editions featuring blue enamel and guilloché dials in 44mm titanium cases, limited to 99 pieces each. 
Why it matters: High horology’s embrace of traditional crafts in contemporary designs reflects enduring demand for artisanal luxury.

Why it matters: As populations age, advances in geroscience could transform healthcare costs and quality of life.

Climate & Environment.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys
Climate & Environment.text: Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answerCape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found that the population had grown by a third since 2000, from 360 baboons to 493, now living in 12 managed troops. Society & Human Rights.title: NEET with a disability: What's holding back visually impaired young people who want to work

Vincent Cassel Transforms Into Quasimodo for Netflix’s ‘The Hunchback, Soul of Paris’
Entertainment.text: SummaryNetflix unveils first-look images of The Hunchback, Soul of Paris.Vincent Cassel leads Jean-François Richet’s 1830-set historical thriller.The film premieres globally on Netflix November 27, 2026.Netflix has unveiled the first-look images for The Hunchback, Soul of Paris, offering an early glimpse at Vincent Cassel’s transformation into the film’s central hunchback figure. The images were first revealed exclusively by Vanity Fair France, introducing the production’s grimy, period-driven vision of 1830s Paris alongside Cassel and fellow cast members Benjamin Voisin, Daphné Patakia and Karim Leklou.Voisin appears as a doctor intent on capturing the protagonist for medical experiments, while Leklou plays the Director of Security leading the pursuit through a city threatened by cholera and political unrest. Rather than leaning into the gothic fantasy or musical elements associated with some previous screen interpretations of Victor Hugo’s The Hunchback of Notre-Dame, the imagery points toward a grounded historical thriller shaped by disease, class tensions and a sustained manhunt.Directed by Jean-François Richet, The Hunchback, Soul of Paris reimagines the life of a man said to have partly inspired Hugo’s Quasimodo, relocating the story to the eve of the July Revolution in 1830 as its protagonist becomes caught between political upheaval, an impossible love and those seeking to experiment on him in pursuit of a cholera cure. The premise draws on archivist Adrian Glew’s theory that Hugo may have encountered a hunchbacked stone carver, though Richet has characterized that connection as a plausible starting point rather than established history. The film reunites Richet with Cassel following Mesrine and The Emperor of Paris, with the wider cast also including Noémie Lvovsky, Sébastien Pouderoux, Eli Nachmani and Alexis Rosenstiehl. Netflix will release The Hunchback, Soul of Paris globally on November 27, 2026.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Breguet Introduces Anniversary “Quai de L’Horloge” Guilloché Dials Across the Marine Line
Entertainment.text: SummaryBreguet refreshes its Marine 5517 and Marine Chronographe 5527.New versions feature hand-guilloché “Quai de l’Horloge” dials.White gold, rose gold and titanium cases span three-hand and flyback chronograph formats.Breguet has unveiled new iterations of two flagship models within its iconic Marine collection: the Marine 5517 three-hand model and the Marine Chronographe 5527. Anchored in the house's historic appointment in 1815 as Watchmaker to the French Royal Navy under Abraham-Louis Breguet, the updated designs balance maritime heritage with modern luxury. Both models introduce subtle architectural updates, such as repositioning the date window to 6 o'clock to enhance dial symmetry, alongside a gold applique at 12 o'clock and signature maritime details like a wave-shaped crown guard and a seconds hand counterweight shaped like the nautical "Bravo" flag.The Marine 5517 keeps the collection at its most streamlined with a 40mm case, three-hand display and date window repositioned to 6 o’clock for greater symmetry. Its gold dial is decorated by hand with Breguet’s “Quai de l’Horloge” guilloché, a motif introduced for the Maison’s 250th anniversary and inspired by both the contours of Paris’ Île de la Cité and Île Saint-Louis and the movement of water. The white-gold edition receives an ice-blue dial, the rose-gold version is rendered in black, and the titanium model adopts blue, with Breguet numerals, “apple” hands and nautical cues including a seconds hand referencing the “Bravo” maritime flag. The 42.3mm Marine Chronographe 5527 develops the same visual language around a flyback chronograph, now using two counters at 3 and 9 o’clock for elapsed minutes and small seconds, alongside the date at 6. Its hand-guilloché dial appears in blue-gradient treatments for the white- and rose-gold models and a grey gradient for titanium.Powering the 5517 is Breguet’s self-winding Calibre 777A, running at 4 Hz with a 55-hour power reserve, while the 5527 uses the automatic Calibre 582QA, pairing its flyback chronograph with a 48-hour reserve. Both watches are water-resistant to 100 meters and expose their movements through sapphire casebacks, where a gold oscillating weight shaped in reference to a ship’s rudder continues the nautical theme.The new models are available through Breguet boutiques and authorized retailers, with prices for the the 5517 ranging from $26,400 USD in titanium on rubber and $30,000 USD on titanium bracelet. Meanwhile the white- and rose-gold editions are $48,900 USD on rubber and $80,300 USD on bracelet. As for the 5527, the model retails between $33,000 USD in titanium on rubber and $36,600 USD on bracelet, rising to $59,400 USD for either gold version on rubber and $93,900 USD on bracelet.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: BAO Celebrates Mid-Autumn With a Guest Chef-Led Moon Festival Menu
Entertainment.text: SummaryBAO celebrates the Mid-Autumn Festival with a special set menu running through October 25.The menu centers on communal platters and guest-chef BBQ skewers.Highlights include Sacha Wagyu BAO, Xinjiang Lamb, Khao Jee Sticky Rice and Moon Face BAO.BAO is extending its Mid-Autumn Festival celebrations into October with a dedicated Moon Festival Set Menu, following the one-day Moon Market held outside BAO Borough on September 24. Drawing on the festival’s traditions of gathering, abundance and communal dining, the menu will be served at BAO King’s Cross, City, Borough and Marylebone from September 29 through October 25, with generous sharing platters intended to be ordered by the whole table. The seasonal program builds on BAO’s Taiwanese-inspired approach to buns and small plates, which has shaped the London restaurant group since founders Shing Tat Chung, Erchen Chang and Wai Ting Chung opened its first permanent Soho location in 2015.Priced at £35 GBP (approx. $46 USD) per person, the set menu opens with an individual Westholme x BAO Grilled Sacha Wagyu BAO, combining North Australian wagyu striploin marinated in umami-rich shacha sauce with braised shallots and daikon pickle. From there, the meal shifts into a communal platter of guest-chef BBQ skewers created by several of BAO’s industry friends. Mambow’s Abby Lee contributes Malay Chipirones, pairing grilled baby squid with squid ink and kaffir lime curry sauce, while culinary artist Nil Mutluer, also known as Heal Goblin, serves Xinjiang Lamb seasoned with cumin, coriander and chilli. Miga’s Mr Ko adds a Korean BBQ Ribeye skewer with sake and pickled celery, and Singburi’s Sirichai Kularbwong looks to a childhood favorite for his Khao Jee Sticky Rice, coating egg-washed sticky rice cakes with Maggi sauce and finishing them with pork floss. Smacked cucumbers, kimchi and lard soy rice round out the shared spread. Dessert continues the lunar theme with BAO’s Moon Face BAO, a special-edition bun filled with salted egg custard.Several elements of the celebration will also be available separately across all BAO locations from September 29, including the Moon Face BAO for £6 GBP (approx. $8 USD), the Westholme collaboration bun for £7.50 GBP (approx. $10 USD) and a Suntory Toki Apple Highball for £10 GBP (approx. $13 USD), developed around citrus, spice and warming autumn flavors. As BAO co-founder and creative director Erchen Chang notes, the wider program interprets Mid-Autumn Festival as a moment of reunion and shared food at the close of the harvest season, a theme reflected most directly in the menu’s table-wide, family-style format.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter Join Tom Holland in Sony Pictures’ Upcoming Fred Astaire Biopic
Entertainment.text: SummaryMargaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter join Tom Holland in Sony’s Fred Astaire biopic.Qualley will play Adele Astaire, while Carpenter portrays Ginger Rogers.Paul King directs the long-developing film, which currently has no release date.Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter have joined Tom Holland in Sony Pictures’ long-developing Fred Astaire biopic, expanding the project’s central trio of performers. Holland remains set to portray the legendary dancer and actor, while Qualley will play his older sister and original stage partner Adele Astaire, and Carpenter will take on the role of Ginger Rogers, the screen partner with whom Astaire became one of Hollywood’s most enduring musical icons.Before his film career, Fred and Adele built a celebrated act together across Broadway and London’s West End, while his later collaborations with Rogers produced some of the defining dance sequences of Golden Age cinema. The casting also places three performers with extensive dance backgrounds at the center of the film, with Holland having previously starred in Billy Elliot the Musical on the West End.The currently untitled film has been in development for nearly five years, with Holland first revealing his involvement in 2021. Paddington and Wonka filmmaker Paul King is directing from a screenplay co-written with Steven Levenson, adapting Kathleen Riley’s book The Astaires: Fred & Adele. King has indicated that the story will place particular emphasis on Fred’s formative partnership with Adele -  whose dancing survives in no known footage - before tracing his emergence as a Hollywood star alongside Rogers. Amy Pascal and Rachel O’Connor are producing through Pascal Pictures, with Holland also producing via his Billy17 banner; Fred Astaire’s daughter Ava Astaire McKenzie is supporting the project, while her son Tyler McKenzie serves as consultant and co-producer.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Vacheron Constantin Introduces a Lighter Shade of Blue to the Overseas
Entertainment.text: SummaryVacheron Constantin celebrates 30 years of Overseas with a 200-piece perpetual calendar.The 41.5mm white gold watch debuts a lighter azure dial, powered by the ultra-thin Calibre 1120 QP/1, which measures 4.05mm and runs until 2100.Vacheron Constantin is marking the 30th anniversary of its Overseas collection with a new Overseas Perpetual Calendar Ultra-Thin, pairing an 18K white gold case with a newly developed azure dial for the first time. Limited to 200 pieces, the anniversary edition builds on a collection first introduced in 1996 as the successor to the Maison’s sport-chic 222, before evolving through subsequent generations in 2004 and 2016. The current Overseas design retains signatures including its Maltese cross-inspired notched bezel and integrated bracelet, while its tool-free interchangeable strap system reinforces the collection’s longstanding emphasis on travel and versatility.Spotlighted at the heart of its dial is a lighter interpretation of Vacheron Constantin’s signature blue. Described as less intense and less saturated than the azure tone first introduced to the collection in 2016, the lacquered dial shifts in appearance according to the light and is paired with a matching blue moon-phase display. White gold hands, markers and calendar indications add contrast without disrupting the monochromatic composition, while blue Super-LumiNova accents aid nighttime legibility. The 41.5mm white gold case measures just 8.1mm thick, and arrives on an integrated white gold bracelet alongside interchangeable white and denim-blue rubber straps, all of which can be changed without tools.Powering the watch is the Maison's self-winding Calibre 1120 QP/1, an ultra-thin 4.05mm movement comprising 276 components and offering approximately 40 hours of power reserve. Its perpetual calendar tracks the date, day, month and leap-year cycle alongside moon phases, automatically accounting for differing month lengths and leap years without requiring correction until 2100. Visible through the sapphire caseback, the Geneva Seal-certified movement features Côtes de Genève, bevelling, perlage and satin-finishing, complemented by a 22K gold rotor engraved with the Overseas compass rose.Priced at $132,000 USD, the new Overseas Perpetual Calendar Ultra-Thin Azure Dial is limited to 200 examples. For more information regarding its availability, head over to Vacheron Constantin's official website.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Brandon Sklenar Goes Full Action Hero in Official Trailer for Western Thriller 'The Rescue'
Entertainment.text: SummaryParamount has released the official first trailer for modern Western thriller 'The Rescue'Brandon Sklenar plays a former rodeo star who embarks on a dangerous retrieval mission after his daughter is kidnapped for a 45 million USD ransomThe action-heavy revenge flick hits theaters on January 29 2027Paramount has unveiled the first official trailer for The Rescue, an upcoming modern Western thriller starring Brandon Sklenar. The high-stakes action thriller feature combines the rugged countryside aesthetic of Yellowstone with the visceral revenge elements of John Wick.The narrative centers on Jamie Lee (Sklenar), a former rodeo cowboy forced to take matters into his own hands when his daughter is abducted and held for a $45 million USD ransom. After a sinister caller targets his ex-wife, country music star Kaley Tucker (Hassie Harrison), with a 48-hour deadline, Jamie realizes local law enforcement is ill-equipped to act.Accompanied by the family's loyal dog, Jamie sets out into a treacherous mountain zone known as "no man's land" to hunt down the captors. The teaser showcases a dark, relentless turn for Sklenar as he uses his horseman skills and survivalist instincts to wage war against a wide-reaching criminal syndicate.The Rescue arrives in theaters on January 29, 2027.Read more at Hypebeast

Science & Technology.title: Black hole jets reach far beyond galaxies' visible edges, potentially deciding their fate
Science & Technology.text: Galaxies are enormous and hold hundreds of billions of stars. These stars form from cold, dense gas. Every large galaxy, including the Milky Way, is wrapped in a huge envelope of gas called the circumgalactic medium, or CGM. This reservoir of raw material stretches 10–20 times the size of the visible portion of the galaxy.

Science & Technology.title: Why earwigs infected by parasitic worms head towards water
Science & Technology.text: Earwigs, small, elongated insects with distinctive pincers at the rear of their abdomens, have little reason to enter open water. While many earwig species are attracted to damp environments, they typically avoid open water. Yet past studies have found that European earwigs infected with a parasitic roundworm called Mermis nigrescens tend to head toward open water. The molecular and biological reasons for this unusual behavior have not been fully uncovered.

Science & Technology.title: Engineers teach spacecraft to 'dream' their way to the space station
Science & Technology.text: Docking with the ISS may seem simple. However, actually doing so shows how difficult orbital mechanics can be. It's like traveling down a highway at 28,000 km/hr (17,000 mph) and parallel parking in an open garage on a multibillion-dollar laboratory traveling at the same speed. If you try to accelerate forward, you actually drift up, and there's no air friction to naturally slow you down. Oh, and if you hit the lab, everyone aboard both your craft and the station dies, and the resulting debris field could wipe out dozens of satellites and even harm people on the ground. No pressure, obviously.

Science & Technology.title: Sparse layers of 10-nanometer silver particles boost CO production from CO₂
Science & Technology.text: Electrolysis can reduce CO2 to CO, a raw material for chemical products such as fuels. Within the GreenQUEST project, an international team led by HZB chemist Prashanth Menezes has systematically investigated catalyst layers made of silver nanoparticles, varying both particle size and density.

Science & Technology.title: A real-time look inside spacecraft heat shields during extreme heat conditions
Science & Technology.text: When a spacecraft reenters Earth's atmosphere at hypersonic velocities, its protective heat shield faces extreme conditions, including temperatures beyond 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,650 degrees Celsius). To survive, the shield relies on specialized materials that absorb heat as they degrade in a controlled process called ablation, sacrificing the shield's outer layers to protect the vehicle and crew within.

Art & Culture.title: Ulysse Nardin Gives the Freak [ONE] Blue Enamel and Guilloché Dial Finishes
Art & Culture.text: SummaryUlysse Nardin expands Freak [ONE] with Blue Enamel and Guilloché editions.Both feature 44mm titanium cases and UN-240 movements.Limited to 99 pieces each, prices start at $80,000 USD.Ulysse Nardin is extending the Freak [ONE] with two limited-edition interpretations that bring traditional decorative crafts into one of the manufacture’s most unconventional mechanical platforms. The Freak [ONE BLUE ENAMEL] and Freak [ONE GUILLOCHÉ] arrive as Ulysse Nardin marks both its 180th anniversary and 25 years since the original Freak debuted in 2001.Of the pair, the Freak [ONE BLUE ENAMEL] places the emphasis on color and métiers d’art. For the first time, the Freak [ONE] is housed in a full 44mm titanium case, framing a white-gold hour disc engraved with a radiating sunray pattern and covered by hand in vivid blue enamel at Ulysse Nardin’s Donzé Cadrans atelier. The enamel is applied in successive layers and fired at approximately 800°C before being polished, creating a saturated surface that accentuates the movement’s rotating flying carousel. By comparison, the Freak [ONE GUILLOCHÉ] adopts a more restrained palette, with its hour disc decorated in a traditional diamond-pattern “maille” motif. The original pattern is created by hand before being transferred to the production discs using the traditional flinqué stamping process, then finished in a sand-toned CVD treatment that contrasts with the light-grey titanium case. The Blue Enamel is paired with a white ballistic-textured rubber strap, while the Guilloché receives a matching grey version.Both watches retain the Freak [ONE]’s UN-240 automatic calibre, whose flying carousel completes one revolution every 60 minutes to indicate the minutes, while the rotating hour disc makes one full turn every 12 hours. Approximately 95% of the movement’s components are designed to move, with its 229-part construction incorporating a silicon oversized balance wheel and hairspring, a DIAMonSIL escapement and Ulysse Nardin’s patented Grinder automatic winding system, delivering a 90-hour power reserve. Time is adjusted through the bidirectional bezel rather than a conventional crown, while the 2026 editions introduce a subtly softened bezel profile inspired by the [Super] Freak.Both models are limited to 99 pieces: the Freak [ONE BLUE ENAMEL] is priced at $89,800 USD, while the Freak [ONE GUILLOCHÉ] retails for $80,000 USD. For more information, visit Ulysse Nardin's official website and boutiques.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
